_meta.name: ID Registry
_meta.purpose: Canonical registry of all prefixed IDs in the spec system. Agents MUST check this registry before creating new IDs. If the needed ID exists, use it exactly. If it does not exist, propose an addition - do not invent on the fly.

naming_rules.general: ALL_CAPS_WITH_UNDERSCORES. Prefix identifies the type. ID must be unique across the entire system.
naming_rules.ITM_: Paintable item. Identifies the PHYSICAL THING being painted. NEVER include phase suffixes (_PRIME, _FINISH) unless the spec family is phase-split AND a collision would occur.
naming_rules.TSK_: Task. Identifies an ACTION performed. Prefix with spec context (e.g., TSK_FRAME_, TSK_DOOR_, TSK_CEIL_) to avoid collisions across specs.
naming_rules.MOD_: SOP Module. Groups tasks into a phase. Prefix with spec context.
naming_rules.SYS_: Material System. A product combination (primer + finish). Tied to quality tiers.
naming_rules.COV_: Coverage Profile. Coverage rates for a material on a surface type.
naming_rules.CON_: Consumable. An expendable item used during work.
naming_rules.VAR_: Variant. A conditional combination of items, methods, and tiers.
naming_rules.IN_: Input. A value sourced from PaintScope. Pattern: IN_{UOM}_{WHAT}
naming_rules.PS_: PaintScope Key. External data source key. Pattern: PS_{CATEGORY}.{SURFACE_OR_ZONE}
naming_rules.SF_: Spec Family. The top-level scope identifier.
naming_rules.ROUND_: Round Configuration. A coat sequence pattern.
naming_rules.COUPLE_: Coupling Constraint. Links two tasks that must run together.
naming_rules.EXCL_: Exclusion Rule. Declares what is explicitly out of scope.
naming_rules.PRIMER_: Specialty Primer. A conditional primer product (knot sealer, etc).
naming_rules.RC_: Research Correction. A corrected finding from research phase.
naming_rules.ISS_: QA Issue. A validation problem found during QA.
naming_rules.XSPEC_: Cross-Spec Flag. A flag passed between specs to avoid double-counting.

SF_STAIR_RISER_NC.notes: Combined prime+paint for stair risers (EA) and stringers (LF). 4 substrates, dual UOM system. First spec with stairwell access modifiers.

SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC.name: New Construction Stair Railing Painting

SF_WOOD_WALL_NC.name: New Construction Wood Wall Panel/Board System Painting
SF_WOOD_WALL_NC.notes: Combined prime+paint for full-height wood wall surfaces (SF). 4 wall_style modifiers. Height varies per room (PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND). 25 tasks, 7 modules.

SF_WOOD_CEILING_NC.name: New Construction Wood Ceiling Panel/Board System Painting
SF_WOOD_CEILING_NC.notes: Combined prime+paint for wood ceiling surfaces (SF). 4 ceiling_style modifiers. ALL work overhead — base rates ~0.70-0.80x of wall equivalents. Height varies (PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND). 30 tasks, 7 modules.

SF_ARCH_ELEMENT_NC.name: New Construction Architectural Element Painting
SF_ARCH_ELEMENT_NC.notes: Combined prime+paint for standalone decorative architectural elements (beams LF, columns EA, mantels EA). 3 paintable items with distinct UOMs. 3 element-specific complexity modifiers (beam_profile, column_type, mantel_type). 39 tasks, 7 modules.

SF_BUILTIN_NC.name: New Construction Built-In Millwork Painting
SF_BUILTIN_NC.notes: Combined prime+paint for built-in millwork (bookcases, entertainment centers, display units). Opening Count method (EA by tier S/M/L/XL) for carcass work. Separate EA item for door/drawer front removal/paint/reinstall. 5 paintable items, 35 tasks, 7 modules. 3 opening modifiers (depth, detail, access).

SF_CABINET_NC_PAINT.name: New Construction Cabinet Painting
SF_CABINET_NC_PAINT.notes: Combined prime+paint for NC on-site cabinet finishing (kitchen, bath, utility). 4 paintable items (door EA, drawer EA, frame SF, interior SF conditional). Door/drawer removal + flat painting + 5-7 day cure + reinstall. 9 protection zones. 5 modifiers (door_style, quality_tier, height, kitchen_complexity, masking_scope). 58 tasks, 7 modules.

SF_WOOD_GRAIN_FILL_NC.name: New Construction Wood Grain Fill (Paint Grade)
SF_WOOD_GRAIN_FILL_NC.notes: Standalone grain fill add-on for open-grain hardwoods being painted. First add-on spec in system. User-activated toggle. QT-driven fill coat count (1/2/3). Surface profile dominant modifier (1.0-2.8x). 6 tasks, 5 modules. Chains: Parent Prime → Grain Fill → Parent Finish. No protection zones.

SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT.name: Exterior Wood Siding Prime and Paint
SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT.notes: FIRST EXTERIOR SPEC. Combined prime+paint for exterior wood siding. 1 paintable item (siding field SF). 3 config dimensions (quality_tier, application_method, siding_profile). 3 factor modifiers (access, substrate_condition, siding_profile). 9 substrate states. 30 tasks, 8 modules. 3 primer + 3 finish material systems. Window/door protection excluded (RC-001). Environmental conditions excluded from estimation (RC-003).

SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC.name: Exterior Fiber Cement Siding Prime and Paint
SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC.notes: Second exterior siding spec. Combined prime+paint for fiber cement siding (James Hardie HardiePlank/HardieShingle/HardiePanel). 1 paintable item (siding field SF). 5 config dimensions (quality_tier QT2-4, application_method spray/brush_roll, siding_profile lap/panel/shingle, surface_texture smooth/cedarmill/roughsawn, substrate_state). 3 factor modifiers (access, siding_profile, surface_texture). 4 NC substrate states. 25 tasks, 8 modules. 3 primer + 2 finish material systems. NO back-rolling on fiber cement. NO power washing. Alkali-resistant primer for bare FC (pH 13.0). Landscape protection LF-based.

SF_.naming_convention: SF_{SURFACE}_{CONTEXT}_{PHASE} where PHASE is optional. Use _PRIME/_FINISH suffix ONLY when prime and finish are genuinely separate spec families (different crews, different sequencing, different bid items). If the spec covers prep through finish in one scope, omit the phase suffix.

ITM_.description: Paintable Item IDs. Identifies the PHYSICAL THING being painted. The item is the constant - tasks are what you do to it.
ITM_.critical_rule: An ITM_ ID represents a physical object, NOT a phase of work. Do NOT create ITM_TRIM_CASING_DOOR_FINISH - the item is ITM_TRIM_CASING_DOOR regardless of whether you are priming or finishing it. The spec family context (SF_..._PRIME vs SF_..._FINISH) already provides the phase.
ITM_.phase_suffix_exception: ONLY use _PRIME or _FINISH suffix on an ITM_ when: (1) the prime and finish specs are separate spec families, AND (2) the same item_id would collide across those families. Even then, prefer no suffix if there is no actual collision risk.

ITM_WINDOW_JAMB.name: Extension jamb / reveal

ITM_STAIR_RISER.name: Stair riser face
ITM_STAIR_RISER.notes: Vertical surface between treads. EA counting sourced from PaintScope Stairwell Geometry System riser count.

ITM_STAIR_STRINGER.name: Stringer / skirtboard

ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL.name: Wainscot panel assembly
ITM_WAINSCOT_PANEL.notes: Single SF item covering panels + internal rails/stiles + base rail + applied molding. Cap rail excluded (ITM_TRIM_WAINSCOT_RAIL). wainscot_type drives complexity modifier.

ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL.name: Wood wall panel/board surface
ITM_WOOD_WALL_PANEL.notes: Single SF item covering board faces, panel faces, internal rails/stiles (library_panel), joint detail (shiplap/T&G), and applied molding. Floor-to-ceiling measurement. wall_style drives complexity modifier.

ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL.name: Wood ceiling panel/board surface
ITM_WOOD_CEILING_PANEL.notes: Single SF item covering panel faces, board faces, joint detail (beadboard/T&G/flat_plank), and coffered beam faces within the ceiling system. ceiling_style drives complexity modifier.

ITM_ARCH_BEAM.name: Decorative beam
ITM_ARCH_BEAM.notes: Running LF of exposed beam length. Profile complexity (width, face count, detail) handled by beam_profile modifier. Typically 3 exposed faces (bottom + 2 sides) for ceiling-mounted beams.

ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.name: Decorative column wrap
ITM_ARCH_COLUMN.notes: Each column counted individually. Size and profile complexity handled by column_type modifier. Height via PS_META.HEIGHT_BAND.

ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.name: Fireplace mantel/surround
ITM_ARCH_MANTEL.notes: Each mantel counted individually. Assembly complexity handled by mantel_type modifier. Typically wall height H1.

ITM_BUILTIN_DOOR.name: Built-in door/drawer front
ITM_BUILTIN_DOOR.notes: Solid doors and drawer fronts removed from built-in unit, painted flat on sawhorses, reinstalled after 5-7 day cure. Glass doors excluded.

ITM_CABINET_DOOR.name: Cabinet door face
ITM_CABINET_DOOR.notes: Cabinet door face — removed, painted horizontally on sawhorses. Style complexity via door_style modifier (slab, shaker, raised_panel, glass_frame). Distinct from ITM_BUILTIN_DOOR and door slab items.

ITM_CABINET_DRAWER.name: Cabinet drawer front face
ITM_CABINET_DRAWER.notes: Drawer front face — removed, painted horizontally. Drawer box interior NOT painted. ~0.7x door time per unit.

ITM_CABINET_FRAME.name: Cabinet face frame and exposed box surfaces
ITM_CABINET_FRAME.notes: Stiles, rails, end panels, toe kicks, filler strips, light valances. Painted in-place after doors/drawers removed.

ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR.name: Cabinet box interior surfaces
ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR.notes: Conditional on scope=full_with_interior. AWI semi-exposed standard — always QT3 regardless of exterior tier. Spray-only.

ITM_GRAIN_FILL_SURFACE.name: Grain fill surface area
ITM_GRAIN_FILL_SURFACE.notes: Aggregated SF from all grain-fill-enabled substrates after UOM conversion. LF→SF 1:1, EA doors via type-based SF lookup, SF direct. First add-on item in system.

ITM_SIDING_FIELD.name: Exterior siding field surface
ITM_SIDING_FIELD.notes: Net paintable siding field area. Profile modifier adjusts effective surface area. Shared across wood and fiber cement siding specs.

SYS_FF_GALLERY.name: Gallery Series Full System
SYS_FF_GALLERY.notes: Architect-spec matched system with dedicated primer

SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC.name: Acrylic Wood Primer
SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_ACRYLIC.notes: Substrate-driven primer for bare wood. Also used for softwood wainscot, wood wall panels, wood ceiling panels, architectural elements, built-in millwork, and cabinet components.

SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_SHELLAC.name: Shellac-Based Knot/Tannin Primer
SYS_PRIMER_WOOD_SHELLAC.notes: Spot primer for knots/tannin bleed on bare wood. Used for pine knot treatment and cherry sapwood on cabinet components.

SYS_PRIMER_ALUMINUM_DTM.name: DTM Etching Primer for Aluminum
SYS_PRIMER_ALUMINUM_DTM.notes: Substrate-driven DTM primer for aluminum windows

SYS_PRIMER_STEEL_DTM.name: Rust-Inhibitive DTM Primer for Steel
SYS_PRIMER_STEEL_DTM.notes: Substrate-driven rust-inhibitive DTM primer for steel windows

SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC.name: Solvent-Based MDF Edge Sealer
SYS_PRIMER_MDF_SHELLAC.notes: Shellac/oil-based edge sealer for MDF cut/routed edges. Step 1 of two-step MDF prime. Water-based causes irreversible fiber swelling.

SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX.name: High-Build Latex Face Primer for MDF
SYS_PRIMER_MDF_LATEX.notes: Step 2 of two-step MDF prime. Face surfaces only — edges already sealed with shellac/oil-based.

SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK.name: Stain-Blocking Primer for Poplar
SYS_PRIMER_POPLAR_STAINBLOCK.notes: MANDATORY for bare poplar. Blocks green mineral streak bleed-through.

SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK.name: Tannin-Blocking Primer for Hardwood
SYS_PRIMER_HARDWOOD_TANNINBLOCK.notes: Blocks tannin bleed-through on bare hardwood (oak, cherry, walnut).

SYS_PRIMER_PLYWOOD_SEALER.name: Standard Primer-Sealer for Paint-Grade Plywood
SYS_PRIMER_PLYWOOD_SEALER.notes: Standard acrylic primer-sealer for plywood surfaces.

SYS_PRIMER_BONDING.name: Bonding Primer for Smooth/Hard Substrates
SYS_PRIMER_BONDING.notes: Enhanced adhesion bonding primer for smooth MDF, questionable factory primers, and hard-to-bond surfaces. Products: Stix, Extreme Bond, Gripper Premium. Recommended (not required) for QT4+ cabinet work.

SYS_GRAIN_FILLER_WB.name: Water-Based Grain Filler
SYS_GRAIN_FILLER_WB.notes: Water-based grain filler (AquaCoat or equivalent) for open-grain hardwoods. Paint-grade only. Coverage varies by grain depth: 60 SF/GAL deep grain, 75 SF/GAL moderate grain. First filler material system (not primer or finish).

SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_ACRYLIC.name: Exterior Acrylic Latex Primer
SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_ACRYLIC.notes: General-purpose exterior primer for new bare wood. Non-tannin species (pine, fir, spruce). First exterior primer system.

SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_TANNIN.name: Tannin-Blocking Exterior Primer
SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_TANNIN.notes: Required for cedar, redwood, and tannin-rich species. Oil-based or shellac-based for tannin bleed block.

SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_BONDING.name: Bonding Primer for Existing Exterior Coatings
SYS_EXT_WOOD_PRIMER_BONDING.notes: For chalking surfaces, semi-transparent stain overcoat, and glossy existing coatings. Enhanced adhesion bridge.

SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_STANDARD.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Latex
SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: Standard production grade exterior finish. 100% acrylic. First exterior finish system.

SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_PREMIUM.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic
SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium residential grade. Superior color retention, fade resistance.

SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_SUPERIOR.name: Superior Exterior Coating
SYS_EXT_WOOD_FINISH_SUPERIOR.notes: Maximum durability. Architect-spec grade. Acrylic or acrylic-alkyd hybrid.

SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ACRYLIC.name: Exterior Acrylic Field Primer for Fiber Cement
SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ACRYLIC.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for field prime over factory primer on fiber cement. Factory prime is transit protection — field prime is MANDATORY per James Hardie warranty.

SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Bare Fiber Cement
SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_ALKALI.notes: Required for bare fiber cement (pH 13.0). Prevents saponification. Reference product: SW Loxon Masonry Primer.

SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_BONDING.name: Bonding Primer for Factory-Finished Fiber Cement
SYS_EXT_FC_PRIMER_BONDING.notes: Required for ColorPlus/ExpertFinish factory-finished surfaces. Oven-baked factory finish requires bonding primer for field paint adhesion.

SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_STANDARD.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Finish for Fiber Cement
SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_STANDARD.notes: 100% acrylic exterior latex. Hardie-approved products (SW Duration or equivalent). QT2 single coat, QT3 two coats.

SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_PREMIUM.name: Premium Exterior Finish for Fiber Cement
SYS_EXT_FC_FINISH_PREMIUM.notes: Premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura — Hardie-approved). Two coats with interstage sand.

surface_ids.rule: Always check Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md before creating a new surface ID. The full vocabulary includes 40+ surfaces across walls, ceilings, trim, doors, windows, cabinets, built-ins, and millwork. Exterior surfaces use ext_ prefix where they would collide with interior equivalents.

zone_ids.description: Protection zone IDs used in protection_zones_required and protection_metadata. Lowercase_with_underscores. Canonical source: Protection_Zones_Reference.md
zone_ids.rule: Always check Protection_Zones_Reference.md before creating a new zone ID. The full catalog includes 28 zones. Note: door_hardware was migrated to hardware_covers in SF_DOOR_SLAB_INT_NC_v1 (2026-02-07).

TSK_.inconsistency_notes: The closet shelf spec uses short generic names (TSK_LIGHT_SAND) while other specs use context-prefixed names (TSK_FRAME_LIGHT_SAND, TSK_DOOR_LIGHT_SAND). Ceiling finish spec uses long descriptive names (TSK_LIGHT_SAND_BETWEEN_COATS_SPRAY). Future specs should use the context-prefixed pattern: TSK_{CONTEXT}_{ACTION}.

MOD_.description: SOP Module IDs. Groups tasks into a phase within a spec.
MOD_.naming_convention: MOD_{CONTEXT}_{PHASE_OR_FUNCTION}. Context should match the spec's shorthand.

VAR_.description: Variant IDs. Conditional combinations of items, methods, and tiers.
VAR_.naming_convention: VAR_{METHOD}_{CONDITION}_{TIER} or VAR_{TYPE}_{TIER}. Should be self-documenting.
VAR_.note: Variants are spec-specific and do not cross-reference. No registry needed beyond naming convention.

ROUND_.description: Round Configuration IDs. Define coat sequence patterns.

COV_.description: Coverage Profile IDs. Material coverage rates by surface condition.
COV_.notes: Only door frame spec currently uses formal coverage profile IDs. Other specs embed coverage rates directly in material_systems. Future standardization should extract all coverage data into COV_ profiles.

CON_.description: Consumable IDs. Expendable items used during work.
CON_.known_inconsistency: RESOLVED (Phase 2 migration 2026-02-07): Closet shelf spec CONS_ prefix migrated to CON_. All specs now use canonical CON_ prefix.

XSPEC_.description: Cross-Spec Flags. Passed between specs to coordinate work and avoid double-counting.

XSPEC_WALL_REPAIR_DONE.description: Set by SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_PRIME when substrate inspection/repair is performed. SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH should skip its first inspection/repair round when this flag is set.

COMP_.description: Composition/Complexity Modifiers. Cross-spec impact when work areas overlap.

COMP_CLOSET_SHELVING.description: Closet shelving presence causes 1.5x modifier on wall/ceiling specs in same closet

FAC_.description: Factor Modifier IDs. Rate-adjusting multipliers for production rate calculation.
